study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier given in the text.

subject_id.notes: Only aggregate cohort statistics reported; no individual subject IDs given.

sample_id.notes: No individual sample identifiers provided in main text.

pmid.notes: PMID not stated within the provided paper text (only external paper_id given).

subcohort.evidence_quote: Seventeen traveled to Central Africa and 18 to the Indian peninsula
subcohort.notes: Two travel-destination subgroups exist (Central Africa, Indian peninsula) but overall data reported at study level.

target_condition.notes: Study examines antibiotic resistance gene carriage in healthy travelers rather than a disease phenotype; no explicit disease/condition term reported.

control.notes: No explicit case/control design; before/after-travel comparison used instead.

country.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
country.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
country.notes: Fecal specimens collected before departure and after return to Sweden; subjects resided in Sweden.

body_site.evidence_quote: fecal specimens from 35 Swedish students taken before and after exchange programs

days_from_first_collection.evidence_quote: The fecal specimens were collected at a median of 4 days before departure (range 0 to 23) and 22 days (range 2 to 120) after return to Sweden.
days_from_first_collection.notes: Aggregate median/range values for two timepoints (before/after) reported, not per-sample days-from-baseline.

location.evidence_quote: Swedish students from the universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg traveling for international exchange studies
location.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

westernized.notes: Not explicitly labeled as westernized in the text, though Sweden is the home country.

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection

dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction kit not specified in provided text; may be detailed in supplemental material.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Sequence data have been submitted to the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB7369.
ncbi_accession.section: Materials and Methods — Nucleotide sequence accession number

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: DNA was extracted from the fecal specimens and sequenced using Illumina HiSeq 2000 technology.
sequencing_platform.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
sequencing_platform.notes: Isolate genomes (ESBL-positive E. coli) were separately sequenced using Illumina MiSeq (250-bp paired-end reads).

age.notes: Reported as a range rather than a single mean/median value.

age_group.notes: Age range 23-34 years falls within Adult classification (>=18 & <65 years).

sex.evidence_quote: with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35)
sex.notes: Reported as an aggregate proportion (74% female, 26/35) rather than a per-subject categorical value.

zigosity.notes: Study concerns Swedish exchange students, not twins.

age_min.notes: Age range reported for entire cohort of 35 students.

age_max.notes: Age range reported for entire cohort of 35 students.

age_years.notes: Only an age range (23-34 years) is provided, not individual or mean ages.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: None of the subjects included were allowed to have taken antibiotics within 6 months prior to fecal sampling.
antibiotics_current_use.section: Materials and Methods — Subject selection and specimen collection
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Confirmed again in Discussion: 'none of the subjects took antibiotics before or during travel.'

disease.notes: Participants are described as health care students traveling abroad; no explicit disease/health status statement provided, though absence of antibiotic use and lack of disease mention suggests they were healthy.

feces_phenotype.notes: Fecal specimens were collected and analyzed for resistance genes/ESBL bacteria, but no explicit stool phenotype term (e.g., consistency, Bristol score) matching schema codes was reported.

fmt_role.notes: Study is not an FMT study.

treatment.evidence_quote: All travelers to Central Africa and 44% (8/18) of travelers to the Indian peninsula used antimalarial chemoprophylaxis.
treatment.notes: Specific agents mentioned in Discussion: mefloquine, proguanil, atovaquone. Usage rate differed by destination (100% Central Africa vs 44% Indian peninsula) but exact per-subgroup breakdown not modeled here due to study_level granularity.

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: genes encoding resistance to sulfonamide (2.6-fold increase), trimethoprim (7.7-fold), and beta-lactams (2.6-fold)
biomarker_name.notes: These were the three most prominently reported significantly increased resistance gene categories after travel; other categories (aminoglycoside, tetracycline, integron, ISCR) also increased but were secondary emphasis.

biomarker_unit.notes: Unit inferred from '-fold increase' phrasing describing the ratio of after/before abundance.

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: genes encoding resistance to sulfonamide (2.6-fold increase), trimethoprim (7.7-fold), and beta-lactams (2.6-fold)
biomarker_value.notes: Table 1 reports slightly different precision (2.61, 7.66, 2.62); abstract values used here as most prominent statement.

disease_response_os.notes: This study concerns microbiome/resistome changes after travel, not survival outcomes.

ecog_performance_status.notes: Not applicable; study population is healthy students, not oncology patients.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No explicit 'feces_phenotype' field defined in the paper; ESBL culture results (e.g., 12/18 India travelers acquired ESBL-producing E. coli) could relate but are not labeled as this schema field.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve tumors.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable; study does not involve tumors.

value: Subjects were 23 to 34 years old, with a gender distribution of 74% females (26/35).

extraction_warnings: This paper reports cohort-level aggregate statistics (means, medians, percentages) rather than per-subject or per-sample data; most subject/sample-level schema fields (subject_id, sample_id, sex, age as single value) cannot be populated at sample_level granularity.

Two travel-destination subgroups (Central Africa, Indian peninsula) exist with some subgroup-specific statistics (e.g., ESBL acquisition rates, antimalarial use), but overall cohort characteristics (age, sex ratio, antibiotics exclusion) are reported only at the study level.
DNA extraction kit and specific sequencing depths per-sample were not detailed in the main text and may require supplemental material review.
PMID and canonical study_name were not explicitly stated within the provided paper text.

This paper is about gut microbiome/antibiotic resistance gene transfer during international travel, not a disease/cancer/FMT/neonatal/obgyn study; most schema fields (disease, tumor staging, FMT, neonatal, obgyn, HLA, zygosity) are not applicable or not reported.

Antimalarial chemoprophylaxis usage differed substantially between the two travel destination subgroups (100% Central Africa vs 44% Indian peninsula), but overall extraction was performed at study_level; subgroup-specific values are noted in the 'notes' field rather than 'by_subgroup'.

Disease/health status of participants was inferred as likely healthy from contextual absence of illness mention and antibiotic exclusion criteria, but not explicitly stated; marked as not_reported to avoid fabrication.

Fields disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size_measurement, and tumor_size_residual_measurement are not applicable to this microbiome/resistome study and are reported as not_reported.

feces_phenotype_value was ambiguous; the paper reports ESBL culture positivity rates but does not explicitly define a 'feces_phenotype' variable, so this was marked not_reported with medium confidence.

biomarker fields were populated using the three most emphasized resistance gene fold-change values from the abstract; Table 1 provides additional resistance gene categories (aminoglycoside, tetracycline, integron, ISCR) with slightly different precision that were not included to avoid over-extraction.
